title: Ishan Kishan's Chepauk Heist: SRH Book Playoff Berth as CSK's Yellow Fades to Grey
excerpt: The left-hander's 70 off 47 guided Hyderabad home with an over to spare, all but ending Chennai's campaign and underlining Sunrisers' credentials as genuine title contenders
body:
At a ground where Chennai Super Kings have long made visiting teams feel like uninvited guests, Ishan Kishan played the role of the intruder who refused to leave. His 70 off 47 balls—composed in its construction, savage in its climax—guided Sunrisers Hyderabad to a five-wicket victory with an over to spare, booking their passage to the IPL 2026 playoffs and all but extinguishing CSK's flickering hopes.

## The Setup: CSK's Fragile Foundation

Winning the toss at the MA Chidambaram Stadium, CSK elected to bat on a surface where first-innings scores above 170 have historically proved competitive. And for a time, it appeared they would post something formidable. Sanju Samson's pyrotechnics at the top—27 from just 13 balls—gave CSK early momentum, and Dewald Brevis's muscular 44 off 27 in the middle overs kept the scoreboard humming. Yet between these bursts lay troubling gaps. Captain Ruturaj Gaikwad laboured to 15 off 21 deliveries without finding a single boundary, a rare display of impotence from a batsman who has been CSK's most dependable run-scorer this decade. Kartik Sharma's steady 32 and Shivam Dube's late cameo of 26 nudged CSK to 180 for seven—a total that felt ten runs short of safety.

The absence of MS Dhoni from the playing eleven, nursing an injury, hung over proceedings like a monsoon cloud. Without his calming presence in the middle order and behind the stumps, CSK's innings lacked the ice-in-the-veins composure that has defined so many Chepauk evenings.

## The Chase: Kishan Takes Command

Hyderabad's pursuit began shakily. Travis Head, the destructive Australian opener, fell for just six, and for a brief moment, the yellow-clad faithful dared to believe. But Abhishek Sharma's aggressive 26 steadied the ship, and when Ishan Kishan strode to the crease, the complexion of the match shifted irrevocably.

Kishan brought up his fifty in 37 balls, a knock of intelligent aggression—rotating the strike when CSK's bowlers hit their lengths, punishing anything fractionally off-line with clean, uncluttered strokeplay. His partnership with Heinrich Klaasen, who himself blazed 47 off 26 deliveries, yielded 75 runs and effectively settled the contest. The pair dismantled Anshul Kamboj's inconsistent spells, with CSK's fielding—including dropped catches—compounding the home side's misery.

Even Samson's moment of individual brilliance—a stumping of Klaasen so swift and instinctive that it drew instant comparisons to Dhoni's legendary glovework—could not alter the match's trajectory. Pat Cummins, leading from the front with three for 28, ensured Hyderabad never lost control of the chase.

## Playoff Implications: Three In, Seven Scrambling

The result confirmed SRH's place in the top four alongside Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Gujarat Titans—the latter also qualifying by virtue of this outcome. For CSK, the arithmetic is now brutal: a maximum of 14 points is attainable, but with their net run rate sliding and only one match remaining (against Gujarat in Ahmedabad on May 21), they are virtually eliminated.

The wider playoff picture remains delightfully chaotic. Punjab Kings sit on 13 points with their campaign complete, watching and waiting. Rajasthan Royals, Kolkata Knight Riders, and even Delhi Capitals retain mathematical possibilities, ensuring the final week of the league stage will be appointment viewing.

## The Diaspora Watches Its Team Fade

For the millions of NRI CSK fans scattered across the globe—from the tech corridors of the San Francisco Bay Area to the trading floors of Singapore, from the university towns of Britain to the suburbs of Melbourne—this defeat carried a particular sting. CSK's fanbase is arguably the IPL's most globally dispersed, built through two decades of Dhoni's charisma and the franchise's relentless consistency. To watch the yellow fade at fortress Chepauk, with Dhoni absent from the field, feels less like a sporting setback and more like the turning of a page.

The IPL remains the single largest cultural appointment for the Indian diaspora's sporting calendar, and this final week—available on JioCinema internationally, Willow TV in the United States and Canada, and FanCode in select markets—will test loyalties and nerves in equal measure. For SRH's growing global following, though, the party is just beginning.
